notes.title: Big UI Update!
notes.notes:
I know iit's been a long time coming, but Auto Fire is back in action and cranking out the updates and improvements!

There has been a major UI revision for just about all of the supporting screens and menus.  Consumable gear was added so you can manually heal up in the field if you have the right items.  There is a significant and growing tutorial that pops up how to play the game as situations present themselves.  (And yes, you can turn them off in the settings!)  More is in the works, including the long-promised arenas, the future looks shiny and chrome this year!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/5af057eefdee7c84574781e402b105555cd34bf4.png[/img]
[h1]Gameplay/Combat[/h1]
[list]
[*] Some garages and repair outlets have a limited amount of gas or ordnance they can sell you.
[*] Consumable gear was created that can repair your internals, drop mines or smokescreens, or basically enact any normal equipment's function.
[*] You can also target yourself on specific sides for armor repair gear, and the UI reflects it on your armor display.
[*] Radar is now a dedicated equipment type and slot called "Sensors".  All cars have a default radar sensors package, but this can do a lot of different things.
[*] AI consider facing when planning their navigation routes, meaning that vehicles will plot paths more naturally and loop around their targets.
[/list]
[h1]Content/Tuning[/h1]
[list]
[*] Old instant repair and armor pickups removed from drops in favor of the repair consumables.
[*] Desert sectors should no longer have random encounters, only emplaced ones (that is, glints and smoke columns rather than just rolling dice)
[/list]
[h1]HUD[/h1]
[list]
[*] Rework of the HUD colors and aiming interface.
[*] Shrank the HUD components (gear, armor, social) slightly to allow for more playable space.
[*] Changed social feed to dark mode, because the bright display was distracting from the gameplay.
[*] Event-based tutorial popups appear when the player experiences various events, from taking damage to skidding to picking up gear.
[*] Added a real date display that updates based on player turns.
[/list]
[h1]Menus[/h1]
[list]
[*] Complete rework of the character and loadout screens.
[*] Complete rework of the repair experience.
[*] Complete rework of the vehicle stable, to show all stats for all vehicles.
[*] Complete rework of inventory, buy and sell screens to add categories and better controls.
[*] Complete rework of the loading dock experience to show a map where you must deliver your chosen item.
[*] New Automap with improved visuals and interactivity.
[*] Entirely new inventory icons, for a punchier and yet colorful look
[*] The loadout view shows pips that indicate when a higher-level item is available to be slotted in that location.
[*] The inventory view shows pips that indicate when an item is new and has not yet been examined.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/54e4e2880c7bf36b0ae6be7c1baf153396a8185b.png[/img]
[h1]Visuals/VFX[/h1]
[list]
[*] Enemy shouts appear in bubbles both on the HUD and over the enemy vehicles in-world.
[*] New power lines, cargo containers, and other assets
[*] Revised fire oil, burning objects and flamethrower VFX
[*] Added decals on the ground from gunfire and explosions.
[/list]
[h1]Audio[/h1]
[list]
[*] Vehicle audio uses Realistic Engine Sounds package and adjusts and shifts gear based on speed.
[/list]

notes.title: October Update!
notes.notes:
Since the [url=https://six.seattleindies.org/]Seattle Indies Expo[/url] at the start of September, I've been hard at work on the core systems of Auto Fire.  This has been in anticipation of showing the game again, this time at the [url=https://roguelike.club/]Roguelike Celebration[/url] in San Francisco this past weekend.  

These folks are all about player choice, so I wanted to make sure I was able to show off different playstyles, and show that the player's choice of car really matters.  That's already the case with the weapon and equipment loadout slots on each chassis, but now there are special abilities baked right in.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/de273f037aa96359e99ab174222029c49aa164d4.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/01e891874affb6d5222e7d946611633774de5393.gif[/img][h1]Speed Perks[/h1]The first vehicular ability is the [b]speed perk[/b], which activates a passive ability whenever you are driving at 60 MPH or over.  These were created for each of the three base cars for different effects:[list]
[*] [b]Ram Blast[/b]:  The Stallion has a speed perk that triggers an explosion whenever it collides at high speed.
[*] [b]Hyperfocus[/b]:  The driver of a Panther gains weapon accuracy at high speed and a higher chance of critical hits.
[*] [b]Jet Wash[/b]:  The Cricket leaves a wake behind it that stuns both pedestrians and 
vehicles, which will careen into obstacles if stunned at the right time.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/63e020c429c7f09902f040870051733dc8cb76ac.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/9726f5d3c399d75c69e77a52b4c78fb2d55e2070.gif[/img][h1]Special Maneuvers[/h1]Each vehicle also has a special move as part of their intrinsic capabilities, providing the player an emergency action they can trigger for major effect.  This does cost valuable gas, however, so use it with care![list]
[*] [b]Ram Piston[/b]:  The Stallion's special maneuver launches forward and bashes through the selected target, knocking it aside.
[*] [b]Jet Thruster[/b]:  The Panther has a special move that thrusts the car ahead at max speed, leaving behind a trail of fire.
[*] [b]Bootlegger[/b]:  Special maneuver that launches forward and spins the car around, ending with a large stunning pulse.
[/list][h1]Updated Gameplay[/h1][list]
[*] Vehicles now consume gas and ordnance as needed by weaponry and equipment.  Gathering resources in the field is necessary for survival, although not all weapons require ordnance... and running out of gas will limit your options but not leave you marooned.
[*] Collisions are now more dynamic, where the heavier or faster vehicle shoves the other aside.  This makes ramming much more satisfying because you can just keep trucking onto the next one if you want.
[*] Controller input has been enhanced to feel better and have better feedback in the UI.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/f80630eb8bb69b5b1a559748a8fbcaa89481fe11.gif[/img][h1]UI and Visuals[/h1][list]
[*] The speedometer and the grip meter has been moved to the bottom center because they are significant aspects to the 
[*] Finally, the Fog of War has had an upgrade.  Because sightlines are limited, there is always a part of the screen that is obscured in some way.  It was time to make that feel less muddy.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35717062/532de1bf4454f034101d6b2ed2b8d145e89a2865.jpg[/img][h1]Onward[/h1]The Roguelike Celebration is a gathering of developers and enthusiasts, and is always an informative and entertaining time...  the best conference of the year by far.  It was awesome to have an opportunity to show them Auto Fire and get their feedback.
The feedback was great, but it was just as inspiring to show off the new features added over the past month.  

So, there's much to do both in response to all the feedback and just to get the game to full-feature status.  The [b]January Kickstarter [/b]is only 13 weeks away...  so I'm looking forward to a productive October!
